signature.why: The two cheap blue-black threats every one of the ten current field lists runs, at 4.0 and 3.7 copies. Frog is the deck: a one-mana body that converts every dead card into a card and a counter, and Riddler is what the deck does with the cards it drew. A build that plays neither is a dimir control deck, which the field files separately.

Cheap black answers. 10/10 field lists run Fatal Push at 4 and Thoughtseize at 3.9; a build cannot be this archetype and answer a resolved threat with nothing, and the split between these five is a metagame call rather than an identity.

The blue half of the same claim. Subtlety and Force of Negation are 10/10 at 3.0 each because a tempo deck holding a 1/3 has to be able to answer a spell on the turn it taps out; which six of these seven a list runs moves with the room.

A dimir manabase. Named rather than counted by colour because the offline cache carries one front-face type line per card, so a colour census is not available here; these seven are the untapped-or-fetch blue-black lands the field's ten lists actually play.

exclude.why: instant reanimator runs the same 4 Psychic Frog, Thoughtseize and fetch manabase and is a different deck with a different guide: it wins by putting Atraxa onto the battlefield on turn two rather than by attacking with a 1/3. Four copies across the pair is the reanimation package, not a splash.
